name: supermarket_cooling_bypass
title: Supermarket cooling system with cooling-coil bypass
summary: Mixed-air air-conditioning of a retail space: outdoor air mixes with return air, part of the mix bypasses a cooling coil with saturated outlet, the streams re-mix and are reheated to the supply state; coil and reheat loads as functions of the bypass fraction.

origin.course: Computer Applications in Engineering Education Vol 1(3), pp. 265-275, 1993
origin.notes: © F-Chart Software / S. A. Klein, MIT via EES-Community/ees-examples. The problem statement is in the Diagram window of the original file; the Diagram window is not imported.

verification.summary: Not the native file (blocked by CS-GAP-PSYCHRO-SAT): the _coolsolve variant was compared with the solution stored in Supermkt.ees and with parametric-table rows 1, 9, 16 (SI by hand). Loads agree within 0.2 %; humidity ratios within 0.5 % (EES vs CoolProp humid air); T[3] within 0.12 %; absolute enthalpies carry a constant ~17.8 kJ/kg dry-air reference offset, differences within 0.16 %.
verification.reference: Solution stored in Supermkt.ees (EES 8.868) and its parametric table Table 1 (ByPass 0 to 0.75), converted to SI by hand; tools/compare_solution.py
verification.notes: 35 common variables, 15 differ (rtol=0.001). All h[i] differ by a near-constant +17.8 to +17.9 kJ/kg of dry air (EES humid-air enthalpy reference vs CoolProp/ASHRAE, h_da=0 at 0 °C); with this offset the enthalpy differences agree within 0.16 % (coil 0.157 %, reheat 0.066 %). Remaining diffs: w[i] +0.24 to +0.45 % (EES vs CoolProp humid-air formulation, as CSL-0028), T[3] 1.21e-03, Q_C 1.93e-03, Q_H 1.03e-03.

related_external: CoolSolve misc/EES_ok.zip and the F-Chart EES example collection (supermkt.ees is a built-in EES example)
